rawData.Lessons Learned: Some security patches have a bug, we need to test it before deploying.

allTickets.description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.

rawData.Impact Details: Incomplete Data Submitted  to the client
rawData.Description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.
rawData.Findings:
The missing profiles were found in the archived files which happens to be the backup file of deleted profiles.

Prior to 2nd half of 2024.  We were not deleting profiles from the TEM.  But due to the TMS license having maximum number of profile definitions.  There came a time where the maximum count is being reached and a need for housekeeping has to be performed.    

The Profile Library Output Report includes a field "Status" indicating that the calling TID record has a physical terminal installed (as retrieved from the ISMS as well)

This became a basis for identifying profiles that can be deleted from the TEM to provide available space for new profiles.

However, per our investigation there are instances where updates on the status are delayed due to external reasons.  Such that profiles get tagged as "No Active Terminal Deployed" thus becoming candidate for deletion or archiving.
rawData.Resolution::
Restoration of the archived profiles in production TEM.
However, need coordination and secure approval from BDO as this might trigger an ADC on the terminals of the restored profile.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Information source on profiles status is not consistent.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Incorrect External Information: Inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading details from clients or external parties causing errors.
rawData.Closing Comments: okay to close as confirmed by Ruel Macapagal

KB5002914 is a Microsoft Office 2016 security update (released in September 2026) that introduced a known bug directly breaking core functions in Microsoft Excel.   
Primary Issues Caused by KB5002914Broken Copy & Paste: Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V) and standard paste actions fail to copy content across cells or sheets.
Broken AutoFill / Drag-Fill: Dragging the fill handle to copy formulas or series across rows/columns either fails, unmerges cells, or corrupts cell formatting.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Some security patches have a bug, we need to test it before deploying.

closedTickets.description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.

rawData.Impact Details: Incomplete Data Submitted  to the client
rawData.Description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.
rawData.Findings:
The missing profiles were found in the archived files which happens to be the backup file of deleted profiles.

Prior to 2nd half of 2024.  We were not deleting profiles from the TEM.  But due to the TMS license having maximum number of profile definitions.  There came a time where the maximum count is being reached and a need for housekeeping has to be performed.    

The Profile Library Output Report includes a field "Status" indicating that the calling TID record has a physical terminal installed (as retrieved from the ISMS as well)

This became a basis for identifying profiles that can be deleted from the TEM to provide available space for new profiles.

However, per our investigation there are instances where updates on the status are delayed due to external reasons.  Such that profiles get tagged as "No Active Terminal Deployed" thus becoming candidate for deletion or archiving.
rawData.Resolution::
Restoration of the archived profiles in production TEM.
However, need coordination and secure approval from BDO as this might trigger an ADC on the terminals of the restored profile.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Information source on profiles status is not consistent.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Incorrect External Information: Inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading details from clients or external parties causing errors.
rawData.Closing Comments: okay to close as confirmed by Ruel Macapagal

reportData.remarks:
The team performed well in both resolving tickets on time and meeting the first-response target.

Target Resolution Time: Met (94.37%) - The team well exceeded the 85% target, showing that active tickets are solved quickly.
Target Response Time: Met (86.08%) - The team met the 85% target for first response.

ISS Binondo handled most of the tickets (49) with strong results (93.88% response and 91.30% resolution).
The response target was missed mainly due to lower pass rates in ECS HRAD (80.00%), ECS ISS MT (50.00%), ECS ISMS Support (80.00% with 4 late responses), ECS PSD (33.33% with 2 late responses).
Once work started, execution was excellent. ECS HRAD, ECS ISS MT, ECS ISMS Support, ECS PSD all achieved a 100.00% resolution pass rate. This confirms the issue is strictly with acknowledging new tickets, not solving them.

Maintain current performance levels and continue tracking both KPIs to sustain compliance across all teams.

routedIncidents.description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.

rawData.Impact Details: Incomplete Data Submitted  to the client
rawData.Description: BDO raised a concern on the Profile Library report wherein TIDs of DX8000 terminals present in the ISMS Deployed Report has no existing records in the Profile Library Report extracted from the different TMS.
rawData.Findings:
The missing profiles were found in the archived files which happens to be the backup file of deleted profiles.

Prior to 2nd half of 2024.  We were not deleting profiles from the TEM.  But due to the TMS license having maximum number of profile definitions.  There came a time where the maximum count is being reached and a need for housekeeping has to be performed.    

The Profile Library Output Report includes a field "Status" indicating that the calling TID record has a physical terminal installed (as retrieved from the ISMS as well)

This became a basis for identifying profiles that can be deleted from the TEM to provide available space for new profiles.

However, per our investigation there are instances where updates on the status are delayed due to external reasons.  Such that profiles get tagged as "No Active Terminal Deployed" thus becoming candidate for deletion or archiving.
rawData.Resolution::
Restoration of the archived profiles in production TEM.
However, need coordination and secure approval from BDO as this might trigger an ADC on the terminals of the restored profile.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Information source on profiles status is not consistent.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Incorrect External Information: Inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading details from clients or external parties causing errors.
rawData.Closing Comments: okay to close as confirmed by Ruel Macapagal

rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit.  These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.   In this case, some of the transactions were included in the CH balance temporarily , even if these were posted to VISA causing the additional amount added to the CH balance. 

Upon checking, the workstation 111.89 doesn't have access on Batch Systems. This caused the OTB matching not to properly match the details between the transactions in Batch and Auth. This caused the incorrect  balances between Batch & Auth

affected records were:
ONG, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5043
BARIA, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-7035
PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013
rawData.Resolution:: The respective network access has been provided  and it has since correctly reflect the balances on the workstation 111.89 since 10/15/2026. Other application and workstations have been check for the connections.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The problem roots from the lack of access of workstation .89 on the Batch Systems. This was the impact during the migration has the access from Binondo to VITRO.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Unauthorized or Improper Access: Access to systems, areas, or data without valid authority, including misuse of credentials.

rawData.Impact Details: The Txn was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. The ECI code pickup was not the correct position.It should pickup position 9-10 instead of 11-12. Pos 9-10 has a value of 07 & pos 11-12 is "02".
rawData.Description: Not Assigned
rawData.Findings:
The transaction was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. 

The POS terminal indicator received an unexpected value  in Field 60 -010000000702  that has 12 digit instead of the usual 10 digit. Thus, the Field 60.8 which is ECI code was erroneously pick up in position 11-12  instead of position 9-10. 

The value of "02" was pickup which is not a valid ECI indicator It should be pick up the ECI code in position 9-10 which has a value "07" non-secure authentication. Other values supporte are 05 and 06.  

05- fully authenticated CAVV Verification submissions
06- used for non-authenticated security transactions at a 3-D Secure-capable merchant. The merchant attempted to authenticate the cardholder using 3-D Secure.

The same logic is applied in the Transaction GUI pos terminal indicator.
rawData.Resolution:: The engine has been modified to correctly pickup the Field 60.8 for the E-Commerce Indicator based on the digit placement of position 9-10 and not the last 2 digit of field 60.   Getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages and ensuring proper handling.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The engine is checking on the last 2 digit of the field 60 instead of the actual digit placement of position 9-10.  Thus, if more than 10 digit was received in field 60, the engine will pick up the incorrect value.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Proper documentation is needed and also, getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages

allTickets.description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.
rawData.Location of the Incident:: Card Production Area, Grou nd Floor, Equicom Center, 3 308 Zapote St., Makati City

affected records were:
ONG,

PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013

closedTickets.description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.
rawData.Location of the Incident:: Card Production Area, Grou nd Floor, Equicom Center, 3 308 Zapote St., Makati City

The team performed exceptionally well in resolving tickets on time, but continued to struggle with initial response speed.

Observations:
ISS Binondo handled the majority of tickets (36 for response, 33 for resolution) with strong performance (88.89% response and 84.85% resolution).
First-response scores were pulled down by specific technician: ECS SDS (0.00%).

Recommendation: Once tickets were assigned, most teams performed exceptionally well, ECS HRAD, ECS SDS, and ECS ISMS Support all achieved 100% resolution pass rates. This confirms the delay is only in acknowledging new tickets, not fixing them.

Incorrect P

The terminal was initially provisioned and downloaded using an incorrect Terminal ID (TID) that did not match the client's actual merchant name.
Due to the incorrect configuration, the merchant successfully processed a live financial transaction under the wrong merchant profile.

rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The FE failed to verify the accuracy of the Terminal ID (TID) against the client's merchant name during the initial terminal configuration and download process.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Reinforce proper TID/profile validation to all Field Engineers before they leave the site to help prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.

rawData.Impact Details: The Txn was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. The ECI code pickup was not the correct position.It should pickup position 9-10 instead of 11-12. Pos 9-10 has a value of 07 & pos 11-12 is "02".
rawData.Description: Not Assigned
rawData.Findings:
The transaction was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. 

The POS terminal indicator received an unexpected value  in Field 60 -010000000702  that has 12 digit instead of the usual 10 digit. Thus, the Field 60.8 which is ECI code was erroneously pick up in position 11-12  instead of position 9-10. 

The value of "02" was pickup which is not a valid ECI indicator It should be pick up the ECI code in position 9-10 which has a value "07" non-secure authentication. Other values supporte are 05 and 06.  

05- fully authenticated CAVV Verification submissions
06- used for non-authenticated security transactions at a 3-D Secure-capable merchant. The merchant attempted to authenticate the cardholder using 3-D Secure.

The same logic is applied in the Transaction GUI pos terminal indicator.
rawData.Resolution:: The engine has been modified to correctly pickup the Field 60.8 for the E-Commerce Indicator based on the digit placement of position 9-10 and not the last 2 digit of field 60.   Getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages and ensuring proper handling.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The engine is checking on the last 2 digit of the field 60 instead of the actual digit placement of position 9-10.  Thus, if more than 10 digit was received in field 60, the engine will pick up the incorrect value.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Proper documentation is needed and also, getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages

routedIncidents.description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.

rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit.  These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.   In this case, some of the transactions were included in the CH balance temporarily , even if these were posted to VISA causing the additional amount added to the CH balance. 

Upon checking, the workstation 111.89 doesn't have access on Batch Systems. This caused the OTB matching not to properly match the details between the transactions in Batch and Auth. This caused the incorrect  balances between Batch & Auth

affected records were:
ONG, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5043
BARIA, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-7035
PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013
rawData.Resolution:: The respective network access has been provided  and it has since correctly reflect the balances on the workstation 111.89 since 10/15/2026. Other application and workstations have been check for the connections.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The problem roots from the lack of access of workstation .89 on the Batch Systems. This was the impact during the migration has the access from Binondo to VITRO.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Unauthorized or Improper Access: Access to systems, areas, or data without valid authority, including misuse of credentials.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Need to thoroughly check the access workstations before the migration activity

rawData.Impact Details: The Txn was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. The ECI code pickup was not the correct position.It should pickup position 9-10 instead of 11-12. Pos 9-10 has a value of 07 & pos 11-12 is "02".
rawData.Description: Not Assigned
rawData.Findings:
The transaction was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. 

The POS terminal indicator received an unexpected value  in Field 60 -010000000702  that has 12 digit instead of the usual 10 digit. Thus, the Field 60.8 which is ECI code was erroneously pick up in position 11-12  instead of position 9-10. 

The value of "02" was pickup which is not a valid ECI indicator It should be pick up the ECI code in position 9-10 which has a value "07" non-secure authentication. Other values supporte are 05 and 06.  

05- fully authenticated CAVV Verification submissions
06- used for non-authenticated security transactions at a 3-D Secure-capable merchant. The merchant attempted to authenticate the cardholder using 3-D Secure.

The same logic is applied in the Transaction GUI pos terminal indicator.
rawData.Resolution:: The engine has been modified to correctly pickup the Field 60.8 for the E-Commerce Indicator based on the digit placement of position 9-10 and not the last 2 digit of field 60.   Getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages and ensuring proper handling.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The engine is checking on the last 2 digit of the field 60 instead of the actual digit placement of position 9-10.  Thus, if more than 10 digit was received in field 60, the engine will pick up the incorrect value.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Proper documentation is needed and also, getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages

allTickets.description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.
rawData.Location of the Incident:: Card Production Area, Grou nd Floor, Equicom Center, 3 308 Zapote St., Makati City

rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit.  These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.   In this case, some of the transactions were included in the CH balance temporarily , even if these were posted to VISA causing the additional amount added to the CH balance. 

Upon checking, the workstation 111.89 doesn't have access on Batch Systems. This caused the OTB matching not to properly match the details between the transactions in Batch and Auth. This caused the incorrect  balances between Batch & Auth

affected records were:
ONG, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5043
BARIA, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-7035
PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013
rawData.Resolution:: The respective network access has been provided  and it has since correctly reflect the balances on the workstation 111.89 since 10/15/2026. Other application and workstations have been check for the connections.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The problem roots from the lack of access of workstation .89 on the Batch Systems. This was the impact during the migration has the access from Binondo to VITRO.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Unauthorized or Improper Access: Access to systems, areas, or data without valid authority, including misuse of credentials.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Need to thoroughly check the access workstations before the migration activity

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.
rawData.Location of the Incident:: Card Production Area, Grou nd Floor, Equicom Center, 3 308 Zapote St., Makati City

rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit. rawData.Impact Details: The Txn was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. The ECI code pickup was not the correct position.It should pickup position 9-10 instead of 11-12. Pos 9-10 has a value of 07 & pos 11-12 is "02".
rawData.Description: Not Assigned
rawData.Findings:
The transaction was declined with response code: 58, Trxn not Permitted to Merchant|E-Commerce Blocked. 

The POS terminal indicator received an unexpected value  in Field 60 -010000000702  that has 12 digit instead of the usual 10 digit. Thus, the Field 60.8 which is ECI code was erroneously pick up in position 11-12  instead of position 9-10. 

The value of "02" was pickup which is not a valid ECI indicator It should be pick up the ECI code in position 9-10 which has a value "07" non-secure authentication. Other values supporte are 05 and 06.  

05- fully authenticated CAVV Verification submissions
06- used for non-authenticated security transactions at a 3-D Secure-capable merchant. The merchant attempted to authenticate the cardholder using 3-D Secure.

The same logic is applied in the Transaction GUI pos terminal indicator.
rawData.Resolution:: The engine has been modified to correctly pickup the Field 60.8 for the E-Commerce Indicator based on the digit placement of position 9-10 and not the last 2 digit of field 60.   Getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages and ensuring proper handling.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The engine is checking on the last 2 digit of the field 60 instead of the actual digit placement of position 9-10.  Thus, if more than 10 digit was received in field 60, the engine will pick up the incorrect value.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Proper documentation is needed and also, getting the more updated and latest simulator will be vital in validating the messages

routedIncidents.description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.

rawData.Impact Details: Prevents dispatch of accurate welcome kits to affected members.
rawData.Description: Clerical oversight on October 14,2026 during mailing process of AXA GHA batch number - BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR the mdb file was miscopied resulting in a mismatch of employee number for 10 axa members.
rawData.Findings:
During the mailing process for AXA GHA batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR on October 14, 2026, an employee number mismatch occurred affecting 10 AXA members on their printed Welcome Letters.
Investigation revealed that during data preparation, two separate batch files were consolidated into a single .mdb database file. During this combination process, the data for batch BATCH-SH-AXAGHA-261013-ZXR was copied incorrectly, causing a field misalignment that shifted the employee numbers for 10 members.
rawData.Resolution:: The combined .mdb file was reconstructed and re-verified against the source master data to correct the data mapping. The welcome letters for the 10 affected members were reprinted and verified before dispatch.  Also, to check if possible to automatate the consolidation of the mDB files.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Human error and manual data handling oversight during the merging of two batch files into a single .mdb file.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Human Error: Mistakes made by individuals due to lack of attention, knowledge, or skill.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Standardized validation check whenever multiple batch files are merged into a single .mdb file. Implement mandatory record-by-record verification for  each merged batch prior to starting print jobs.
rawData.Closing Comments: Able to identify the cause of the error.
